title: GPU supply curve and order-phasing plan
content:
Purpose and summary:
This working doc proposes a supply-curve driven procurement and phasing approach for our GPU fleet across regions (US-W, US-E, EU, APAC). Goal: smooth capital outlays, reduce lead-time risk, and keep production utilization in the target band (65–75%) while preserving a rolling buffer for growth and failover.

Why supply-curve + phased orders?
- Vendor lead times vary dramatically by SKU and quarter; single large buys concentrate risk.
- We need predictable per-quarter capacity additions to support Dedicated reservations and hosted API SLAs.
- A supply-curve (mixing long-lead high-performance SKUs with short-lead mid/low-cost SKUs) gives flexibility to cover near-term demand while positioning for long-term throughput.

Key assumptions (baseline model):
- Q4-2024 baseline committed throughput demand: 280M tokens/day across hosted + dedicated workloads.
- Target steady-state production utilization: 70% average (windowed over 30d).
- Safety buffer: 15% of usable vRAM-equivalent capacity for unexpected spikes and region failover.
- SKU options considered: NVIDIA H100-80GB (H100), NVIDIA A100-80GB (A100), NVIDIA L4-24GB (L4) and used-gpu pool (refurb, variable).
- Effective vRAM equivalence: H100=1.0, A100=0.7, L4=0.18 (for LLama-style throughput mapping used in our model).

Lead-time & procurement characteristics (vendor/region averaged):
- H100: lead time 14–22 weeks; MOQ constraints; higher price volatility; delivery phasing typically in 2 shipments.
- A100: lead time 8–12 weeks; reliable volumes from primary OEM partners; mid price volatility.
- L4: lead time 4–8 weeks; good spot availability from cloud OEMs; suitable for burst/edge regions.
- Refurb pool: variable lead-time 2–10 weeks; lower cost, higher failure rate.

Supply-curve rationale (example mix):
- Long-term backbone (H100): 35% of new committed vRAM-equivalent capacity per year. These are committed early (buy windows), good for heavy-attention workloads where latency matters.
- Medium-term fill (A100): 45% of additions; lower lead time and cost tradeoff for steady throughput.
- Short-term elasticity (L4 + refurb): 20% of additions; used to absorb burst growth and maintain target utilization with fast delivery.

Order-phasing policy (conservative plan):
- Rolling 6-quarter pipeline with monthly reviews.
- Trigger for placing a tranche: projected utilization for any region > 72% in the next 12-week lookahead OR committed reserved capacity uptake > 10% quarter-over-quarter.
- Tranche composition: each tranche ~20–30 GPU units of mixed SKUs sized to cover ~4–6% of global additional capacity depending on SKU mix.
- Lead-time buffer: we place H100 tranches at least 20 weeks ahead of the quarter they are intended to serve; A100 at 10 weeks; L4 at 6 weeks.

Regional adjustments and constraints:
- EU: customs cycles add ~2 weeks effective lead time; prefer earlier A100 orders and higher L4 short-term allocation to avoid long customs exposure.
- APAC: limited H100 availability windows; strategy is to shift more of the long-term backbone buys into US-E/US-W and replicate via Dedicated placement where possible.
- US regions: prioritize H100 mix for west coast region where low-latency customers are concentrated.

Scenario model outputs (illustrative numbers for Q1–Q4 next fiscal year):
- Growth scenario (20% YoY demand increase): need +360 vRAM-equivalent units; phased orders: 35% H100 (~126 equiv), 45% A100 (~162 equiv), 20% L4/refurb (~72 equiv).
- Flat scenario (5% increase): need +90 vRAM-equivalent units; compress orders into fewer tranches, lean on L4/refurb for short-term.
- Downturn scenario (demand -10%): pause H100 buys, cancel/deferral clauses exercised for upcoming tranches, re-route capacity to multi-tenant pools.

Risk register and mitigations:
- H100 supply shock: maintain an extra 8% global buffer (reserve tranche) and prioritize workloads for H100 to customer tiers with SLA.
- Shipping/customs delays: pre-clearance documentation and early vendor notification; re-allocate L4 capacity to impacted region while waiting.
- Exchange rate spikes: include FX collars on >$500k purchase orders when lead time >12 weeks.
- PSU/cooling lead time mismatch: align rack-level components procurement schedules with GPU delivery windows in each tranche.

Operational checklist and owners (next 12 weeks):
- Confirm Q1 demand forecast window with product analytics (owner: Priya Singh) – due 2024-10-20.
- Vendor negotiation: lock A100 price bands for Q1 tranches (owner: Lucas Moreno) – negotiation start 2024-10-25.
- Legal: update standard PO with deferral and partial-shipment acceptance terms (owner: Legal Ops, Elena Volkova) – draft 2024-11-05.
- SRE/Rack readiness: map cooling/power per data center to H100 arrivals (owner: Infra SRE lead) – readiness checklist 2024-11-30.

Action items (short list):
- Build a simple supply-curve simulator in the procurement repo that inputs: SKU lead times, price curves, region quotas, projected demand; output: suggested tranche schedule and PO sizes. (owner: Michael Chen, repo link in linked artifacts)
- Create a rolling calendar with monthly gating meetings between product, infra, and finance to decide tranche placements. (owner: Priya Singh)
- Prepare 2 alternate buy scenarios tied to FX and vendor allocation changes (owner: Lucas Moreno).

Open questions for discussion in procurement sync:
- How aggressive should we be using refurb GPUs as a structural short-term solution vs a temporary stopgap?
- Acceptable customer impact policy when we elect to prioritize H100 capacity to dedicated enterprise customers during constrained windows.
- What is the stretch budget for an opportunistic H100 buy if a favorable vendor window opens unexpectedly?

Appendix: simple reorder trigger pseudocode
- if projected_utilization(region, 12 weeks) > 0.72:
    compute shortfall = projected_demand - committed_capacity*usable_factor
    tranche = size_from_shortfall(shortfall)
    place_purchase_order(tranche, sku_mix_for_region(region))

Notes and provenance:
- Demand numbers based on internal usage telemetry (prod token counts) and Dedicated committed seats pipeline (private forecasts).
- Lead-time numbers from vendor scorecards (internal procurement dataset) aggregated across Q2–Q4 2024.

Document status:
- Draft – intended as working plan to discuss with procurement/finance and the prod analytics owner. Expect multiple iterations once the monthly capacity sync runs in Oct 2024.
